source.docs: The repository is the source of truth. This catalog points at it; it never duplicates a procedure.
source.versions: compatibility/version-matrix.md — parsed at build time, so a version bump propagates without touching this file.
source.adr: decisions/ADR-*.md — the reasoning behind every option below.

methods.title: Bare metal
methods.summary: Physical servers, direct disks for Ceph and etcd, full control of PCIe and NUMA topology.
methods.bestFor: Ceph at scale, GPU inference, predictable IO latency, no hypervisor in the failure path.
requirements: IPMI or BMC access for out-of-band installation
Local SSD for etcd, dedicated NVMe for the Ceph OSD DB and WAL
RAID1 for the boot disk, or software RAID managed by the OS baseline

methods.title: Virtual machines
methods.bestFor: Small sites, lab and staging, environments without hardware.
requirements: Ceph OSD disks must be raw or SCSI-passthrough, never a shared virtual disk
etcd on a local SSD with dedicated vCPUs, never on shared storage
GPU needs passthrough; MIG is not virtualizable, so pass the whole card
The hypervisor joins the failure domain and must be in the DR plan

methods.title: Cloud-init
methods.summary: User-data provisioning via cloud-init; OS and host baseline applied from an internal mirror.
methods.bestFor: Nodes booted from an internal image repository where cloud-init is available.
requirements: cloud-init enabled image in the internal mirror
User-data reachable from an internal web server
Host baseline applied before cluster bootstrap

methods.title: PXE network boot
methods.summary: PXE boot from an internal TFTP/HTTP server; unattended OS install with kickstart/preseed equivalent.
methods.bestFor: Large fleets of bare-metal nodes provisioned from a single internal PXE server.
requirements: Internal DHCP + TFTP + HTTP PXE server
PXE-enabled NIC on every node
Boot image and kickstart/preseed file on the internal mirror

methods.title: Kickstart
methods.summary: Red Hat Kickstart automated installation from an internal HTTP repository.
methods.bestFor: RHEL/AlmaLinux/Rocky node fleets installed from an internal mirror.
requirements: Internal HTTP repository with Kickstart tree
Kickstart file referencing internal packages
Boot media or PXE chainloading the Kickstart config

methods.title: Ansible automation
methods.summary: Existing nodes prepared and bootstrapped with Ansible playbooks from the automation directory.
methods.bestFor: Sites that already run Ansible and want host baseline + kubespray inventory from playbooks.
requirements: Ansible control node reachable from all targets
SSH key or break-glass account on every node
automation/ansible playbooks committed to the repo

clusterMethods.title: Kubespray (Ansible)
clusterMethods.summary: Version-pinned inventory, idempotent, offline-capable, five releases supported in parallel.

clusterMethods.title: kubeadm
clusterMethods.summary: Kubernetes native bootstrap tool; version-pinned control plane and node join, air-gap capable with internal registry mirrors.
clusterMethods.bestFor: Conformance-focused clusters and teams that want the upstream K8s bootstrap tool.
requirements: kubeadm, kubelet, kubectl pinned to one Kubernetes version on every node
Containerd configured with the internal registry mirror
Control-plane endpoint (VIP or LB) reachable before kubeadm init

clusterMethods.title: RKE2
clusterMethods.summary: Rancher's enterprise Kubernetes distribution; single-binary, CNCF-certified, built for air-gapped and offline installs.
clusterMethods.bestFor: Rancher-managed sites and air-gapped production clusters wanting a single-binary distro.
requirements: RKE2 install script reachable from an internal mirror
SELinux/AppArmor tuned for RKE2
ETCD and control-plane nodes sized per Rancher sizing

clusterMethods.title: Talos
clusterMethods.summary: API-managed, immutable Linux for Kubernetes; no SSH, OS and K8s upgraded together via talosctl.
clusterMethods.bestFor: Teams wanting an immutable, API-driven OS with minimal attack surface.
requirements: talosctl on the management machine
PXE or iPXE boot or an installer image per node
Control-plane endpoints defined in the Talos machine config

clusterMethods.title: kind
clusterMethods.summary: Kubernetes IN Docker; runs K8s nodes as Docker containers. Local/dev only, not for production.
clusterMethods.bestFor: Local development, CI, and conformance testing on a single machine.
requirements: Docker running on the host
kind binary installed
Local loopback networking sufficient

clusterMethods.title: MicroK8s
clusterMethods.summary: Snap-packaged, single-node-to-cluster Kubernetes; small footprint for edge and CI.
clusterMethods.bestFor: Edge nodes, CI runners, and small air-gapped footprints.
requirements: snapd available on every node
MicroK8s snap from an internal mirror or snap proxy
Cluster mesh or single-node

clusterMethods.title: OpenShift
clusterMethods.summary: Red Hat enterprise Kubernetes platform; operator-centric, licensed.
clusterMethods.bestFor: Enterprises with Red Hat subscriptions wanting an integrated platform.
requirements: Red Hat subscription and pull secret
Installer-provisioned infrastructure (IPI) or user-provisioned
OpenShift installer and ignition configs

pages.title: Deployment
pages.subtitle: Where this platform runs, and what it is called.

pages.title: Management cluster
pages.subtitle: Rancher or an alternative management UI, optional in-cluster storage, Keycloak and the directory integrations, sized separately from the workload clusters.

pages.title: Application cluster
pages.subtitle: Control plane, Linux and Windows workers, and the resources kept for the OS and the agents. Additional application clusters are added one at a time, each with its own CIDRs and sizing.

pages.title: Operating system
pages.subtitle: Common OS baseline (all roles). Role-specific overrides live in the tabs below — master, worker, Ceph OSD/MON, load balancers, operation server and others.

pages.title: Storage
pages.subtitle: Rook inside the cluster, or cephadm on dedicated hosts with one node group per Ceph role.

pages.title: Traffic
pages.subtitle: Edge load balancer, L7 ingress and in-cluster L4.

pages.title: Network and offline artifacts
pages.subtitle: Address plan, CoreDNS forwarding, registries and package repositories. Everything is mirrored; nothing is pulled from the internet.

pages.title: Platform services
pages.subtitle: GitOps, secrets, observability, policy, mesh and GPU. Optional components can be switched off.

pages.title: Add-ons
pages.subtitle: Optional cluster components, each with its own values file and its own line in the deploy script. They install in the order listed in addons/platform-addons.md.

pages.title: Port requirements
pages.subtitle: Server-to-server access request: the firewall flows this configuration needs before any node is handed to Kubespray.

portRequirements.dstSubnet: L7 ingress (F5 NGINX IC / NGF / Envoy)

options.title: Oracle Linux 8
options.warning: Kernel 4.18 is below the 4.19 recommendation in the Kubespray kernel matrix.

options.title: 5 control-plane nodes, stacked etcd
options.warning: Longer maintenance windows, and a third failure domain is needed to justify it.

options.title: Calico — mature, rich policy, IPIP/VXLAN
options.note: Calico is configured through the Kubespray inventory for the pinned release.

options.title: cephadm on dedicated hosts — Podman
options.note: Upstream default engine. No container engine dependency inside Kubernetes.

options.title: cephadm on dedicated hosts — Docker
options.warning: Supported but second-class upstream. Pull the engine from the internal mirror; docker.io on Ubuntu is too old.

options.title: HAProxy (L4, active health checks) + Nginx (L7, TLS), Keepalived, Docker Compose
Nginx only (L4 passthrough + L7), Keepalived, Docker Compose
F5 NGINX Gateway Fabric (Gateway API native)
Envoy Gateway (Gateway API native, second implementation)

components.title: Directory integration
components.note: Application-level only. Nodes are never joined to a directory. Keycloak brokers OIDC so each service speaks one dialect.

options.title: OpenBao (MPL 2.0)
options.note: The deployment model is portable from Vault. Use it when the BSL is not acceptable.

options.title: No central logging (not recommended for production)
Velero with CSI snapshots to object storage
Istio ambient (ztunnel per node, waypoints where L7 is needed)
options.note: Lower per-pod cost, but a ztunnel fault affects every pod on the node.

options.title: Istio sidecar (Envoy per pod)
options.warning: Adopt only when the threshold in service-mesh/evaluation.md is met. Adds a control plane and a failure domain.

options.title: GPU workers with MIG isolation and vLLM serving
GPU workers with time-slicing (development only, no VRAM isolation)
options.warning: No memory isolation between pods. Never for multi-tenant production.

options.title: cert-manager with a Vault PKI ClusterIssuer
cert-manager with a self-signed bootstrapping issuer
options.warning: Bootstrap only. Remove it once the Vault issuer works.

options.title: Metrics Server (required by HPA and VPA)
Auto mode (evicts and restarts pods)
options.warning: Never for stateful workloads. Restarts pods on every recommendation change.

options.title: Eviction enabled
options.warning: Respects PodDisruptionBudgets. Every eviction is a restart someone must explain.

options.title: Trivy Operator with an internal DB mirror
No storage in the management cluster

values.hint: Assigned in order: control plane, then workers, then GPU.

Edge nodes

values.hint: Serves github.com/, dl.k8s.io/, storage.googleapis.com/, get.helm.sh/ for the offline Kubespray deploy.

values.label: Additional registries (one per line)
values.hint: Keep the upstream repository path so no manifest rewrite is needed. One entry per line.

values.label: Additional package repositories (one per line)
values.hint: RPM, deb, PyPI, npm or Helm. Format: type name url

values.label: Registry credentials (base64 user:password)
values.hint: Leave empty and fill it on the target host. Rendered locally into the downloaded file only.

values.label: VRRP authentication pass phrase

values.label: Passwordless sudo for the automation user
Extra kernel arguments
values.hint: Example: intel_iommu=on iommu=pt for GPU passthrough. Requires a reboot.

values.label: Transparent huge pages
values.hint: never for Ceph OSD hosts: THP stalls show up as slow ops.

values.label: Security-only unattended updates
values.hint: Never let them reboot a node silently; drain first.

values.label: Rook OSD worker nodes
values.hint: Workers that carry an OSD disk. The rest stay storage-free.

values.label: Kubernetes version override
values.hint: Empty uses the release default. Never skip a minor on an upgrade.

values.label: Ceph release
values.hint: The repository you mirror decides the exact build; this records the intent.

values.label: Ceph container image override
values.hint: Empty uses the distribution package. Only set a pinned digest when the mirror requires it.

values.label: CoreDNS upstream servers
values.hint: Space separated. Cluster DNS forwards everything outside cluster.local here.

steps.title: Confirm the requirements, assumptions and open decisions
actions: Close every open decision
Confirm the IP plan and the failure domains
Confirm the legal position on the Vault license

steps.title: Read the architecture and the decisions
actions: Review the architecture overview
Review the failure-domain table for the components you selected

steps.title: Stand up the internal repositories and mirror every artifact
actions: Deploy Harbor and Nexus
Mirror every artifact for the selected components
Verify offline install, image pull and chart deploy on a throwaway node

steps.title: DNS, NTP, network, PKI, load balancing
actions: Deploy DNS and NTP
Create the internal CA and distribute the trust bundle
Deploy the edge load balancer
Implement the firewall rules from the matrix

steps.title: Automation server, Ansible, AWX, GitLab, Vault
actions: Install Ansible in a virtualenv with the pinned version
Deploy AWX and register the runners
Deploy Vault on dedicated hosts and test the unseal procedure

steps.title: Provision and harden the nodes
actions: Configure the internal repositories
Apply sysctl, kernel modules and the security baseline
Confirm the local break-glass account and key work with no network dependency
Install the monitoring and logging agents

steps.title: Deploy the storage platform
actions: Create the CRUSH map with the host failure domain
Create the pools, the filesystem and the object store
Confirm Ceph HEALTH_OK before consuming any volume

steps.title: Deploy the application cluster with Kubespray
actions: Fill the inventory and the group vars from the generated files
Mirror the artifacts for the selected Kubespray release
Run cluster.yml, then validate the control plane and etcd

steps.title: Join the Windows node pool
actions: Calico is the CNI: confirm kube_network_plugin is calico before the Windows play runs
WinRM over HTTPS reachable from the Ansible host, account in the local Administrators group
Container runtime and the Containers feature installed on every Windows node
Same Kubernetes minor as the control plane; the generated vars pin kube_version
No Ceph RBD on Windows: keep stateful workloads on Linux

steps.title: Build the extra application clusters
actions: Each cluster needs its own pod and service CIDR, API VIP and inventory
Run deploy.sh again with that cluster's nodes.tsv and k8s-cluster.yml
Register each cluster in Argo CD with its own Secret, labelled secret-type=cluster
One ApplicationSet per cluster so a bad sync cannot reach the other clusters

steps.title: CNI, ingress, load balancing, CSI
actions: Install the CNI and confirm kube-proxy replacement
Configure MetalLB and the ingress controller
Configure the CSI driver and the StorageClasses
Apply the Gateway API CRDs

steps.title: Deploy Istio and enable mTLS in stages
actions: Confirm the adoption threshold in service-mesh/evaluation.md is met
Extract and mirror every image the install and the dataplane need
Decide the dataplane mode: ambient (per node) or sidecar (per pod)
Install the control plane with Helm so Argo CD owns it
Apply PeerAuthentication STRICT to one namespace, watch metrics, then continue
Apply the default-deny AuthorizationPolicy only after the allow rules exist
Test a negative case: a pod that should be denied must be denied
Wire Istio telemetry into the existing Prometheus stack

steps.title: Rancher, Keycloak, Argo CD, backup
actions: Deploy the management cluster from its own inventory
Install Rancher and register the application cluster
Install Keycloak and wire OIDC for each service
Install Argo CD and sync the first application
Install Velero and run a first backup

steps.title: Integrate the directory at the application layer
actions: Confirm the break-glass local account works with the directory unreachable
Create a read-only bind account and store its credential in Vault
Configure Keycloak user federation first, read-only
Create one OIDC client per service with explicit redirect URIs
Wire services in order: Argo CD, Rancher, Harbor, GitLab, Vault, Kubernetes API
Remove the local superuser path only after a federated admin login is verified
Alert on failed federated logins and on a zero-login drop during working hours

steps.title: Vault integration, admission policy, runtime detection
actions: Bind the Vault role to the service account
Deploy the admission controllers in audit mode, then enforce
Enable the runtime detection ruleset
Verify certificate renewal and secret rotation

steps.title: Metrics, alerting, logs
actions: Install the monitoring stack and confirm every target is up
Configure the alert routes and the runbook links
Deploy the log pipeline and prove the redaction filter

steps.title: Install the selected add-ons in dependency order
actions: cert-manager first: every TLS-dependent add-on needs an issuer
Metrics Server, then VPA, then the descheduler
external-dns last, after the edge VIP exists
Trivy Operator with a mirrored vulnerability DB, never an internet download
OpenTelemetry Collector only when a trace backend accepts OTLP
Validate: kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io, kubectl get certificates -A, kubectl get clusterissuer

steps.title: GPU workers, driver, sharing, serving
actions: Install the driver and the GPU Operator
Configure MIG and verify the isolation
Mirror the model weights and start the inference server
Validate the DCGM metrics

steps.title: Pipelines, approval gates, drift detection
actions: Wire the pipeline stages
Protect the branches and require the approvals
Turn on the nightly drift job

steps.title: Upgrades, backups, restore, disaster recovery
actions: Run the upgrade procedure on a staging copy
Restore into a scratch namespace and measure the RTO
Rebuild a node from the OS and Kubespray
Exercise the full rebuild order offline

steps.title: Acceptance tests and handover
actions: Execute every acceptance test and store the evidence
Record the known limitations
Hand over to the operations team

steps.title: Give users working access from Linux and Windows
actions: kubectl and kubelogin on the user machine: winget on Windows, the signed binary on Linux
One kubeconfig per user or group with the OIDC exec plugin; never a shared client certificate
Merge into KUBECONFIG, never overwrite ~/.kube/config
Automation tokens come from kubectl create token with a short duration, stored in the CI secret store
Verify: kubectl auth whoami, kubectl get nodes, kubectl auth can-i --list
